notes:
Video Studio adds Storybook cartoon for scripted movies. It draws eight distinct images per second, holds each for three frames in a 24 fps MP4, and can animate an eight-second shot in one batch. It keeps the original canvas and all sixteen standard sampling steps. This produces the stepped timing of limited animation. Existing Cartoon and Cinematic styles retain their original motion cadence.

The same four-second image-conditioned shot on an RTX 3060 12 GB took 4 minutes 1 second at the regular cadence and 2 minutes in Storybook cartoon. Both tests used the same seed, scene description, reference image and resolution. These are single-shot measurements. Actual movie times include voice recording, scene changes and final mastering. After a completed episode the time estimate can learn from that PC's own results.

Screenplays of one minute or longer now keep verified shots through a pause or interruption. Replacing a soundtrack of matching duration on a compatible H.264 video now preserves the original picture packets at the same size, avoiding another lossy encode. Automated tests covered exact picture preservation, silent and voiced 24 fps mastering, UI estimates, pause/resume and an end-to-end 184-second test using controlled footage. Source commit 0cc83058e35f87bdff3cc8e04bf63e48116a6b14.
A full-length trial exposed a native progress limit at the first shot over four seconds. The corrected build accepts up to eight seconds in the new style. The ordinary cartoon limit and validation of out-of-bounds updates remain covered by tests.
A separate test attached a matching soundtrack to the same 16-second clip. Including full output verification, the previous path took 1.86 seconds and changed the picture packets. The new path took 1.15 seconds and preserved those packets exactly.
